label: Every actual root has every pure perfection, from no unexplained absence
description: Fix an actual root r at w and a pure k. By excluded middle r has k or lacks it. If r lacks k, no unexplained absence at actual roots says no admissible profile contains r's determinations and k. The root's profile is admissible and k occurs in some admissible profile. The structural L bridge then gives r a represented limiting principle, which the existing statement that actual roots have none excludes. So r has k. The main theorem uses no axioms; the Comparator companions use the three Mathlib axioms. structuralControls (one carrier, source true the only actual root) witnesses every premise and the conclusion, and gives for four of the five non-logical premises an assignment where it fails, the other premises hold and the conclusion fails; anchorControl does this for the fifth. Where no unexplained absence fails, the source's lack of noesis is unexplained; where the L bridge fails, joint compossibility fails and the lack is a positive exclusion; where admissibility of each pure determination fails, noesis is in no admissible profile; the finite-mode rows have a nonpure limiter. anchorControl has an infinite all-pure root profile and finite admissible profiles: only admissibility of the root's profile fails. standingRival puts the no-unexplained-absence failure on the same source as the #1892 impersonal eminence model and shows a personal source lacking the admissible pure a violates the same premise. The models are assignments of the stated relations, not metaphysical possibilities.
